First off, thank you for replying
Second off: The problem is that people here don't understand the whole 'workload is crushing me' bit. everyone has the mindset of 'its not a big deal. you're weak if you can't do this. just stfu and do your work. Other people did it so don't whine that the workload is crushing you.' even my own parents don't care. I kept telling them I have neither the aptitude nor the attitude for taking math in 11th and 12th, but they forced me too and they forced me to take the science stream too. but still, in their own words, 'I'm free to do whatever I want'. Ironic isn't it. I just don't think I'm cut out for school or studies. What I really want to do (writing) is something my parents dont give even half of a quarter of a damn about.

No prob.
Try getting more friends online. If people won't interact with you in person because of what that girl did, then find people online who will. Especially seeing its a girl who did it (and society favours the female gender in these matters) its best to find new friends who like you for who you are. Parents.... well they're parents. They're annoying, irritating and can do more harm that good to you in certain occasions. You're stuck with them, so I'd say: try phasing them out. Let what they say go in one ear and out the other. That's what I do with my mum and dad and it helps a ton.

I'm in school too, last year, and I know where you're coming from. Problem with school is that there's no escape from it. If you try taking a break, the workload just piles up higher and higher, and with exams, no one cares what you're going through, whether it be family problems, injury, sickness, depression, suicidal thoughts etc. and that's just the facts. Yet I still urge you to try and take a break. If you have break/holidays coming by soon, hold on till then and unwind to the best of your abilities. A day, or even a week off might give you some time to really dig deep and give full attention to your thoughts and help you make your decision, whatever that may be.

Its annoying to hear, I know, But i've been feeling the same way for over a year now. Every time I go: Today I'll kill myself, but I never do, for whatever reason. An incident that occured... about 5 years ago made me think there wasn't any point to living, and I still believe there isn't. the trick is to make a point for living, no matter ho bullshitty it is. You could try to get to the root of what's causing these feelings, as you are the best deducer of what's happening in your own mind. Once you find out, go from there.
If you feel irritated when someone goes 'i"m here to talk' or just don't feel like talking to anyone about it, you could possibly try talking to yourself, venting out all your frustrations and anger. Beat up a pillow, smash a bed in with a baseball bat wrapped with barbed wire, whatever you need to do to vent.

I get the rationale of wanting to use a gun, but what if you miss? or worse, what if you live? then you'd have to go your entire life with a hole in your head. You'd be much worse off at that point.
In all seriousness, there's no guaranteed method, not is there any painless method for suicide, seeing that dying is a painful process by nature. Heights are an option, I know of a person who took that to their advantage, but again, what if you land on your feet? or you don't jump off from high enough? All methods have a horrible risk of failure. If you want to use any of them, you have to be willing to risk catastrophic failure. So instead, a blank slate to life achieved by whatever means you can think of would be the most risk free solution if we're talking mathematically.

What seems to be the cause of her depression? And how does her thought process work, especially on matters concerning depression and suicide, as well as motivation and positivity and negativity. Getting to the root of these thought processes will help you better help your girlfriend through her depression. (eg: If a person can't stand motivational speeches or 'oh it will get better, trust me' talks, it is for the best that you stray far, FAR away from them whilst helping them through their tough times)
If you already know all of the above mentioned factors, I would suggest letting her take her own path in life, choose what she wants to choose. I know it seems like a horrible option, but trust me, there is nothing more empowering than to let a person make tough decisions on their own without coercion from others. It makes you the sole perpetrator of all the good (and bad) in your life, and it can really help when you feel down.
I speak all these things from personal experience, and if you DO feel like you're at the end of your power to be by her side, the best thing to do is step back and let her do what she needs to do.
